whatTheLiveBytesSay: D-000 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md line 20) is titled 'Delegation protocol adopted'. Read in full, it records: adversarial subagent review to consensus (clause 1), a 3-turn termination clause (2), register documentation (3), commit-and-push per decision (4), and PREFERENCE-LADEN marking (5), plus a sequencing note, reversibility and commit lines.
The string 'owner' does not occur anywhere in D-000, case-insensitively. D-000 records no product-owner process.
What D-000 does record is the opposite actor: 'the assistant completes the coop design end-to-end, making coordinator/product-authority decisions on the user's behalf'.
The row's own owner cell (file 08 line 299, cell 2) is 'Product owner'.
The subject's own carried source text says so too: boundaryTextCarriedVerbatim.linesVerbatim[12] = 'acceptance, product owner DR-117 must explicitly disposition:' (file 02 line 283).

The lane's standing discipline is that owner authority is user-made, not coordinator-composed: D-096 'This entry does not make the coordinator those owners'; D-097 'Withdraw the coordinator-composed C2 owner grant'; D-100 'Authority is a later user-made D-096 (A) grant, not this entry' and 'Mechanics alone never grants.'
shouldFix.defect: Deleting the D-096 (A) prerequisite was correct — I independently established at v1 that D-100 clause 3 limits eligibility to the five D-096 artifacts and that DR-117 is not among them, so (A) was never the applicable gate for this row. The defect is in what replaced it. Calling the substitute 'the recorded D-000 product-owner process' asserts a recorded provenance that does not exist, which is the same defect class Codex flagged at PBSCV1-S1 (calling D-066 owner recording when D-066 says 'An ACCEPT verdict is not owner recording'). v2 cured that instance and introduced the class in the adjacent sentence. The direction also reverses: v1's error was conservative — it named an extra gate — while v2's removes the only named user-express gate for a row whose owner is the product owner, and points instead at the very protocol under which the assistant decides on the user's behalf.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing is authorized or recorded. The artifact binds NOTHING, is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and DO-NOT-SEAL, mints no grant, states three times that it does not, and the DR-117 row remains OPEN. Any later disposition would need its own D-000-reviewed entry judged on its own bytes. The error is in describing the route, not in taking it.
shouldFix.provenanceNote: The identical phrase appears in Codex v1's PBSCV1-S2 minimumRepair ('route any later DR-117 disposition through the recorded D-000 product-owner process, with MF-6 if file 08 is changed'), so v2 followed the instruction it was given. That explains the defect but does not cure it: this is a review of the subject's bytes, and the claim is in them.
shouldFix.repair: Drop 'recorded' and the 'D-000 product-owner process' construction. State instead that DR-117's owner is the product owner per file 08 cell 2 and file 02 line 283; that this artifact records no route and creates none; and that D-096 (A) is not the applicable prerequisite because DR-117 is not one of the five D-096 candidates D-100 clause 3 makes eligible.
